**1. Sudo probe** (non-interactive, so it can't hang on a password prompt):
```sh
whoami; id
sudo -n -l 2>&1
```
Look for `NOPASSWD:` entries and for sudoable commands that are themselves escalation vectors (e.g. `sudo /usr/bin/vi`, `sudo /usr/bin/find`, `sudo /usr/bin/python`, `sudo /usr/bin/awk`, `sudo /usr/bin/env`, `sudo /usr/bin/less`, `sudo /usr/bin/tee`, `sudo /usr/bin/dd`, `sudo /usr/bin/ssh`).

**2. Setuid/setgid scan:**
```sh
find / -xdev \( -perm -4000 -o -perm -2000 \) -type f 2>/dev/null -exec ls -ld {} \;
```
Common interesting ones: `pkexec` (CVE-2021-4034 PwnKit), `sudo` (version-dependent), `newgrp`, `su`, `passwd`, `mount`/`umount` (can be abused with crafted fstab), `at`, `crontab`, `chfn`/`chsh` (if they point at a shell).

**3. Worth checking alongside:**
```sh
# sudo version (known vulns)
sudo -V | head -1
# writable sudoers
ls -ld /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null
# pkexec version (PwnKit)
pkexec --version 2>/dev/null
# capabilities on binaries
getcap -r / 2>/dev/null
```
